issues.legal_issue: The effect of a delayed declaration under a housing-acquisition scheme on the validity of the acquisition and the compensation payable.
material_facts: A housing board initiated an acquisition under a statutory scheme, with scheme notices serving the role of acquisition notices and later notices serving the role of declarations.
The declaration was issued more than three years after the initial scheme notice.
The board took possession and constructed housing colonies, and purchasers were living in the houses when the cases were decided.
issues.conclusion: The opinions differed on whether the three-year limit applied: Justice Ramaswamy held that it did not apply because the relevant acquisition provisions were incorporated into the local law, while Justice Sahai held that it did apply. The common operative order did not quash the acquisitions; it directed that compensation be calculated using the market value in the year the declaration was issued, treating that year as the year of a fresh notification.
issues.legal_principle: Justice Ramaswamy applied the incorporation-by-reference distinction: under Section 55 and the Schedule to the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965, the relevant provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 were incorporated with modifications, so later amendments to the central Act did not automatically become part of the local law. He relied on Secretary of State v. Hindustan Cooperative Insurance Society Ltd., State of M.P. v. M.V. Narasimhan, Bolani Ores Ltd. v. State of Orissa, and Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd. v. Union of India, and distinguished Bhatinda Improvement Trust v. Balwant Singh. He also held that Article 254 did not invalidate the local law because the laws could operate in their respective fields. Justice Sahai read the local law as applying the Land Acquisition Act by reference, relied on Bhatinda, and concluded that the time limit applied. The common remedial order preserved the acquisitions in view of the completed housing projects and the public interest in avoiding displacement and loss to residents.

rule.if: housing_scheme_acquisition and delayed_declaration and completed_housing_project and homes_occupied_by_purchasers

predicates.housing_scheme_acquisition: A public authority acquired land through a housing or improvement scheme governed by a special statutory procedure.
predicates.delayed_declaration: The declaration completing the acquisition process was issued after the period allowed by the generally applicable acquisition procedure.
predicates.completed_housing_project: The acquiring authority had taken possession and constructed a housing project on the acquired land.
predicates.homes_occupied_by_purchasers: People who had purchased homes in the project were living in them when the challenge was decided.

issues.definition: When a housing-scheme acquisition has a delayed declaration but the project has been built and occupied, the acquisition is preserved and compensation is adjusted by reference to the declaration year.

issues.legal_issue: The scope of issues that may be considered in an appeal where leave was limited to a specified question.
material_facts: Leave to appeal was granted only on the question whether the three-year limit applied to acquisitions under the local housing law.
Counsel sought to raise additional grounds that were not within that question.
Some constitutional writ petitions were later tagged with the appeals.
issues.conclusion: Justice Ramaswamy declined to hear additional grounds in the limited-leave appeals, except grounds concerning jurisdiction or constitutional validity. Justice Sahai stated that the separate writ petitioners should not be barred from pursuing issues other than limitation in an appropriate forum; the final order preserved that opportunity for the writ petitioners.
issues.legal_principle: The Court emphasized consistency, certainty, and comity in respecting the question on which leave was granted, while recognizing jurisdictional and constitutional-validity exceptions. Justice Sahai distinguished independently admitted writ petitions from appeals whose leave was expressly limited and stated that the writ petitioners could pursue other issues in an appropriate forum.

predicates.limited_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which permission to appeal was confined to a specified legal question.
predicates.proposed_issue_outside_granted_question: A party seeks a decision on an issue beyond the question for which permission to appeal was granted.
predicates.issue_affects_jurisdiction_or_constituti: The additional issue concerns the court's jurisdiction or the constitutional validity of the challenged provisions.

issues.definition: In an appeal limited to a specified question, an additional issue outside that question is not heard unless it concerns jurisdiction or constitutional validity.
